item.title: Fighter jet gestures: Umpire celebrates with Pakistan team after controversial Asia Cup win; India questions neutrality
item.description: The Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI) has questioned the neutrality of a Pakistani umpire after a video appeared to show him celebrating with Pakistan players through gestures that seemed to mimic aircrafts crashing. The incident has added to the tensions between the two teams following the controversy over the rain-hit Men's Asia Cup for the Blind final in Dhaka. India's blind cricket team had boycotted the trophy presentation ceremony after Pakistan were declared champions despite the final being washed out without a ball being bowled. CABI has now raised concerns over the umpire's conduct, saying match officials must remain neutral and should not be seen celebrating with either team. “This Pakistani umpire officiated throughout the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind 2026, yet is seen celebrating with the Pakistan team,” CABI said in a statement. “As per the principles of officiating, an umpire must remain neutral and should never be seen aligning with any team,” the association added. — blind_cricket (@blind_cricket) The latest row follows Pakistan being awarded the title on the basis of a superior run rate after rain prevented the final from taking place. India had argued that both teams should have been declared joint winners, as there was no reserve day, instead of deciding the title through net run rate. The controversy grew after World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) president and Pakistan Blind Cricket Council chief Sultan Shah reportedly overruled the WBCC Technical Committee's recommendation to declare India and Pakistan joint winners. The match referee was then directed to announce Pakistan as champions. CABI general secretary Shailendra Yadav accused Pakistan of unilaterally declaring themselves champions, alleging that the decision disregarded the position of the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee. "I am deeply disappointed and strongly condemn the manner in which Pakistan has declared itself the winner of the Blind Cricket Asia Cup final without a single ball being bowled," Yadav said in a statement. In protest, the Indian players stayed away from the trophy presentation ceremony.

Speaking after Los Blancos' latest La Liga fixture, the Portuguese tactician emphasised that having the 22-time Grand Slam champion in the club's hierarchy carries deep personal meaning . item.title: Australia defeat frustrates Wales head coach Tandy
item.description: Wales head coach Steve Tandy said he was frustrated as his side failed to back up their epic win over New Zealand, narrowly losing to Australia. The Wallabies edged the Nations Championship Test 29-26 in Cardiff, a week after a first Wales victory over the All Blacks since 1953 had led to wild celebrations. Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau secured a try-bonus point for Australia as Ryan Lonergan and Carter Gordon added nine points with the boot. Wales also scored four tries, through Dewi Lake's double, Blair Murray and Ryan Elias, with Sam Costelow landing three conversions. However, they fell agonisingly short. "The overarching feeling is the frustration of losing," said Tandy. "We were disappointed. We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been. We were held up three times and could have gone ahead on the scoreboard." Tandy added: "Maybe we needed a little bit of composure but there were enough opportunities to come away with the win. "I know it's not the result anyone wanted but the supporters were amazing again." Despite the loss, and that frustration, the Wales head coach praised his side's attitude in attempting to follow up their historic win against the All Blacks. "Fair play to the boys, after such a monumental game last week with the emotional energy, we stuck in the game and scored four tries," he said. "So there are a lot of positives in the performance to take as well." Australia hold on for narrow win against Wales Nations Championship - Australia triumph over Wales - reaction Highs and lows of sport - Lake Dewi Lake has scored three tries in the past two internationals [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Australia, having soaked up fierce first-half pressure, produced some fine attacking rugby after the break to prevent Wales from winning three matches in a row for the first time since the 2023 World Cup. "It's sport, you have major highs and then lows, and that's the game we play," said skipper Lake. "Our frustration comes from the fact that we probably weren't at our best. "We created opportunities during large parts of the game, but there were little inaccuracies at the wrong times." Lake, however, said he could not fault the effort of the squad. "We spoke about backing up last weekend, and we didn't back it up with a result but I think we backed it up with effort and energy," said the captain. "We had opportunities to win that game, but unfortunately it wasn't to be for us today. "We'll fix those accuracy issues and we'll be ready to go again next week." Wales will face Japan at the Allianz Stadium at Twickenham on Saturday after both sides finished fifth in the two Nations Championship tables - north and south. It will be a fifth time Wales and Japan have met in 16 months with Tandy's side defeating Eddie Jones' team 28-21 in Cardiff just two weeks ago. item.title: Ohio State Staring In The Face Of A Fifth Loss With Michigan Coming Up
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Things go from bad to worse for Ohio State, as Michigan has all the momentum heading into a big showdown. Nothing is going right for Ohio State football at the moment. The Buckeyes fell to 7-4 on the year with a 31-28 loss to Nebraska. The win finally got Matt Rhule a landmark victory, while also moving the record for the Huskers to 7-4 – the same as Ohio State. Related: Iowa Football Makes Statement Regarding College Football Playoff Rankings While it was a remarkable win for Nebraska, it was just as big of a loss for the Buckeyes. Especially considering the next opponent up. Ohio State Has Zero Momentum Heading Into Matchup With Michigan Things have gone from bad to worse for the Buckeyes since losing Julian Sayin. They are out of the Big Ten Conference race, and can now pretty much say so long to any chance they had of reaching the College Football Playoff. Michigan, meanwhile, stunned UCLA to give Kyle Whittingham’s bunch momentum. And honestly, right now, they might be better off than the Buckeyes. Luke Fahey did not look bad, he just did not look like a superstar at quarterback for Ohio State. Fahey threw for 259 yards and two TDs, as Bo Jackson ran for a pair of scores. But the Buckeyes averaged just 3.5 yards per rush and under 10 yards per pass. Jeremiah Smith provided 165 yards and two touchdowns on six receptions, but outside of the Heisman Trophy contender, there was little to be happy about. Would Ohio State Move On From Ryan Day With A 7-6 Season? You would think Ryan Day’s job is secure. But in the current state of college football, does anyone really ever feel safe? Day has had critics in the past, but he has found a way to get Ohio State to the promised land and quiet them over and over again. Would those same naysayers grant him an out with Sayin injured? If the Buckeyes fall to Michigan, they would have lost four of the final five to close out the regular season. And that is not a great way to enter the postseason. Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: Kimani Johnson thrives as Mizzou takes down Auburn, advances in SEC Tournament
item.description: Mizzou volleyball is moving on in the SEC Tournament after taking down Auburn 3-1 Friday night in Savannah, Georgia. The Tigers (15-10) earned the four-set victory with scores of 25-23, 25-19, 22-25 and 25-20. The win also provided a measure of redemption for Mizzou, which is back in the SEC Tournament quarterfinals after falling to Ole Miss in the first round of last year’s tournament. Kimani Johnson led the way with a monster performance, recording 17 kills on 37 attacks while hitting .270. She added three solo blocks and three block assists, finishing with 19.5 points to lead all players. K-monster thrives Johnson’s performance was a testament to the improvement she has made throughout the season. The fifth year was a consistent presence in the Tigers’ offense, delivering when Mizzou needed an answer and making her presence felt at the net. Her six total blocks also helped anchor a defensive effort that limited Auburn to a .169 hitting percentage. Paige Felder provided another major contribution with 14 kills on 33 attacks, hitting .333. Lauren Larkin was particularly efficient, putting away eight kills without an error on 12 attempts for a .667 hitting percentage. Setter Nina Mandovic orchestrated the offense with 29 assists. Mizzou opened the match by narrowly taking the first set 25-23 before building momentum with a 25-19 second-set victory. Auburn responded in the third, escaping with a 25-22 win to extend the match. The Tigers answered in the fourth, using a strong offensive finish to secure the 25-20 set and close out the match. The Tigers finished with 54 kills and six total blocks. Auburn managed 43 kills but struggled to find consistency, hitting just .169 compared to Mizzou’s .172. Mizzou now turns its attention to Vanderbilt, which it will face Sunday night in the SEC Tournament quarterfinals. The Tigers already have a win over the Commodores this season, giving them another opportunity to carry regular-season success into postseason play. With a spot in the semifinals on the line, Mizzou will look to build on its performance against Auburn and keep its tournament run alive.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama seemingly takes ‘stat padding’ dig at Luka Doncic after latest 50-point game
item.description: Credit: Alex Goodlett/Ezra Shaw via Getty Images Speaking after yet another historic performance this season, Victor Wembanyama looked to take aim at Luka Doncic as the MVP race between the two stars heats up. Wembanyama scored 50 points against the New Orleans Pelicans, marking his second 50-point game this season, with the first coming a little over three weeks ago. It was a dominant showing from the French superstar, who currently finds himself in a heated MVP battle with Luka Doncic. Victor Wembanyama claims he isn’t as good at ‘stat padding’ as his ‘peer’ Luka Doncic Speaking after his historic performance against the New Orleans Pelicans, Victor Wembanyama was asked about reaching the 50-point mark yet again. He then joked that he should have delivered such scoring performances more frequently, and then claimed that, unlike his peers, he isn’t good at stat padding. “It is very special,” Wembanyama told DAZN. “Unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding. So, I haven’t reached it as many times as I should have.” Understandably, many in the NBA community believe this was Wembanyama poking fun at Luka Doncic, who has been accused of staying in games longer than he needs to in order to try to keep his numbers high. However, Doncic’s defenders have pointed out the drastic drop-off in the Lakers’ offence whenever the superstar exits the game early, and how that gives the coaching staff no option but to make him re-enter the game. So far this season, Doncic is averaging 37.2 points while shooting 46.8% from the field and 37.6% from beyond the arc this season. Wembanyama’s scoring exploits haven’t been anywhere close, as he is averaging 29.9 points while shooting 54.1% from the field and 31.5% from deep. The two are considered the favourites to win the MVP award this season, especially as both the Lakers and the Spurs are currently tied for the best record in the NBA, along with the Philadelphia 76ers. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The New York Knicks survived a dramatic finish against the Portland Trail Blazers , escaping with a 97-96 victory after Mikal Bridges delivered the game-winning shot. Jalen Brunson led the way with 30 points, including six three-pointers, while Bridges added 12 points and came through when it mattered most. It was an ugly, hard-fought game for much of the night, but the Knicks found a way to get the job done. New York’s biggest advantage came from beyond the arc. The Knicks knocked down 19 of 42 three-point attempts (45.2%), compared to Portland’s 11 of 38 (28.9%). That shooting gap proved decisive in a game where the Trail Blazers actually won the rebounding battle 47-42 and outscored New York 48-26 in the paint. The Knicks also had a commanding 26-point lead at one stage, only to let Portland back into the contest. Brunson’s scoring and Bridges’ late-game heroics ultimately saved New York from a frustrating collapse. Here is how every Knicks player performed. Jalen Brunson: A Game Stats: 30 PTS, 7 REB, 5 AST, 3 TOV, 11-23 FG, 6-10 3-PT FG, 2-3 FT, 36 MIN Brunson was the engine behind New York’s offense, delivering a 30-point performance with six three-pointers. He was particularly effective from deep, converting 60.0% of his attempts, and consistently gave the Knicks a scoring option when their offense needed a spark. His seven rebounds and five assists added to an otherwise strong all-around performance. Three turnovers and a relatively inefficient 11-for-23 shooting line prevent this from being a perfect grade, but Brunson was clearly the Knicks’ most important offensive player. New York needed every one of his 30 points. Landry Shamet: A Game Stats: 20 PTS, 1 REB, 3 AST, 7-14 FG, 6-10 3-PT FG, 36 MIN Shamet delivered one of his best performances of the night, matching Brunson’s perimeter shooting with six made three-pointers of his own. He finished with 20 points on 50.0% shooting, providing the Knicks with a second major scoring threat. Even more impressive was his ball security. Shamet finished without a single turnover while adding three assists. His minus-three plus/minus was not ideal, but his shooting was instrumental in helping New York build its sizable lead. The Knicks needed his offensive production, and he delivered. Mikal Bridges: B+ Game Stats: 12 PTS, 2 REB, 3 AST, 1 STL, 3 TOV, 5-8 FG, 2-3 3-PT FG, 28 MIN Bridges did not have the same scoring workload as Brunson or Shamet, but he made his biggest contribution when the game was on the line. His game-winning shot gave New York a victory that had become increasingly difficult to secure after the Knicks surrendered their large lead. He was efficient from the field, making five of eight attempts and two of three from beyond the arc. Three turnovers and a minus-six rating are negatives, but the value of delivering the decisive basket cannot be overlooked. Bridges came through in the moment that mattered most. item.description: In college football, bragging rights are almost worth as much as trophies. Yes, after an eight-year drought (which was preceded by an 11-year drought), winning three straight national championships was a huge deal for the Big Ten. But while the hunk of metal that Michigan (2023), Ohio State (2024) and Indiana (2025) got to take home is nice to look at, the element that’s unique to college football is being able to tell the SEC “We’re better than you” and having a scoreboard back it up. At least at the top of the league, the Big Ten was better than the SEC for three straight seasons. Winning the College Football Playoff with three different programs, while the SEC wasn’t even represented in the championship game, made it inarguable. It was fresh and exciting for a league that couldn’t hold a candle to the SEC’s success in the modern era. But now, thanks to a crazy run of quarterback injuries, it’s over. Yes, the Big Ten will have a representative in this year’s CFP. But after UCLA’s expensive loss to Michigan and Indiana’s puzzling performance at Washington , there’s now a scenario where the Big Ten is a one-bid league and doesn’t even come within sniffing distance of the championship game. Talk about evacuating the penthouse. As we sit here after the penultimate week of the regular season, it’s fair to say the Big Ten’s four best teams this season were Oregon, Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA. All four will end the season with major quarterback problems that almost certainly will crush their chances of a deep run. Let’s take them in sequential order. On Sept. 26, Oregon’s Heisman contender Dante Moore suffered a concussion after a dirty hit by USC’s Desman Stephens and hasn’t played since. Oregon went into a nosedive and fired the offensive coordinator but has played better since. At 8-3 and ranked No. 13, however, the Ducks have a very narrow path to a playoff bid. Near the end of Ohio State’s 19-15 win at Indiana on Oct. 17, Julian Sayin took an awkward hit that caused a significant arm injury . Freshman Luke Fahey wasn’t ready to take his place, but the Buckeyes’ problems are deeper than one player. They’ve spiraled on both sides of the ball and are completely out of the mix now at 7-4 after a 31-28 loss at Nebraska . Indiana’s Josh Hoover has been banged up for much of the season, and at times backup Grant Wilson has looked more effective. While the result alone was noteworthy given Miami’s star-studded roster featuring Lionel Messi, Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez, Casemiro, and others, the incident involving Messi that has drawn significant criticism from fans and media is currently generating the most discussion. It happened in the 47th minute, after the referee added five minutes of stoppage time to the first half. Lionel Messi Draws Criticism for Controversial Throw-In Against Columbus Trailing 1-0 and already down to 10 men after Gonzalo Luján’s 36th-minute red card, Messi attempted a quick throw-in but threw the ball directly into an opposing player’s face (Gonzalo Tapia). Watching the footage closely, it is difficult to determine whether Messi did it intentionally. However, the situation was fairly straightforward: he could have waited for the referee to let him take the throw-in properly. Debates surrounding the incident are inevitable, but what matters most is hearing your opinion. item.title: Maple Leafs Seem to Have Lost Faith in Sergei Bobrovsky
item.description: Sergei Bobrovsky Maple Leafs Artur Akhtyamov Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs seem to have lost faith in their high-profile offseason addition, Sergei Bobrovsky. Anthony Stolarz got the call against the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday night at Scotiabank Arena, marking the second straight for the 32-year-old. And after the way things went in their game against the Chicago Blackhawks last week, there is little reason to believe that the organization feels Stolarz is their best bet to win. While the decision to go with Stolarz may be nothing more than a practical one aimed at giving Bobrovsky some time off, the fact is that the situation in Toronto has gotten too loud to ignore. The Maple Leafs are desperate to get back into the win column. And the bulk of the chatter has placed a fair part of the blame on Sergei Bobrovsky’s shoulders. That’s why it shouldn’t be surprising to see the Leafs going with this plan for now. Of course, the organization will need to make a long-term decision regarding Bobrovsky. If this is just a temporary blip, fans should see the veteran netminder back in the crease sooner rather than later. But if this is a sign of things to come, the Maple Leafs may need to make a permanent call on Bobrovsky before the season really gets away from Toronto. Toronto Knows It Can’t Push Anthony Stolarz Too Hard While Anthony Stolarz is a capable netminder, the Maple Leafs know they can’t push him too hard The Leafs know that, as good as Stolarz can be, fatigue and injury issues arise when he’s asked to shoulder a load for too long. That much was evident last season. That is why Sergei Bobrovsky should find himself back in the crease within the next couple of games. The Maple Leafs may be trying to take some pressure off their veteran netminder while allowing him time to reset mentally. If that is the case, giving Stolarz a short run of starts makes sense. It allows Toronto to keep chasing points while Bobrovsky works through what has been a difficult stretch. However, the organization cannot allow that short-term plan to turn into a permanent game plan. Stolarz has proven capable of handling important minutes, but Toronto’s ideal scenario was always a tandem approach. The Maple Leafs figured that playing Stolarz about once a week was going to be the right load management. That’s why the organization needs to resist the temptation to suddenly dump the bulk of the starts on their backup goalie. Maple Leafs Really Have No Other Choice With Sergei Bobrovsky The reality of the matter is that the Maple Leafs don’t really have much of a choice with Sergei Bobrovsky. Toronto doesn’t really have any other way forward. A trade is not a realistic solution, especially with Bobrovsky’s contract and recent performance creating obvious obstacles. Sending him to the minors is not a practical option either. That leaves the Maple Leafs with one path forward: They have to work through this. item.title: Wojo: Wolverines, Whittingham fight back. Can they do it again in Columbus?
item.description: ANN ARBOR — Kyle Whittingham and the Wolverines earned respect and applause, and for what it’s worth, likely a bowl bid. Those all count for something, and they’ll count for even more if they follow up with a victory in Columbus next Saturday. But did they earn more time? It’s the question that will linger after another pulsating, final-play outcome, almost as improbable as all the others. The Wolverines handed No. 4 UCLA its first loss, piling drama on top of drama in an 18-16 triple-overtime victory Saturday, Nov. 21, in Michigan Stadium. The home season ended as it began, with a walk-off score and a spontaneous field-storming by the crowd. Whittingham hasn’t had many signature moments here, and I’m not sure one is enough. It’s enough to suddenly make The Game — downgraded this year to “the game” — a hotter stew of debate and discord. Whittingham’s job security rightly is under scrutiny, especially with a new athletic director, Trev Alberts, on the way . Michigan is 6-5 with seven of its games decided on the final possession. Fighting past the Bruins , who were 10-0 and one of two unbeatens left in the country, was gutty and laudable. Meanwhile, the Buckeyes are 7-4 after losing to Nebraska, and Ryan Day is getting heat, just two years removed from a national title. What once appeared to be a rivalry blowout looks much more intriguing now. The Buckeyes have collapsed since quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an injury. And no matter how many times UM’s offense collapses, its defense keeps rising. Whittingham indeed may have bought time, and not just because UM should be headed to a bowl game. Many of us had him fired before Alberts even showed up, and the outcry is understandable. But it’s also why, in today’s crazy college football, you have to let it play out. (Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Kirby Smart’s Georgia Bulldogs did not have their best stuff this evening in Columbia. In the beginning that looked like a problem. In the end, that fact was a little comforting. Why? Because even though they missed some tackles, didn’t take control of the line of scrimmage until late, and squandered some plum scoring opportunities, they were still four touchdowns better than a top 25 South Carolina team, pulling away with 31 unanswered points for a 34-6 victory. Things started off with that queasy feeling Bulldog fans have felt before in Williams-Bruce. The Gamecocks matriculated the ball steadily down the field to score on their opening drive. Georgia managed a field goal to tie it, then gave up another agonizing drive punctuated by a pair of LaNorris Sellers third down runs that ended in three more points. The Gamecocks matriculated fans were loud and proud. The Bulldog offensive line was catching more than driving. And Sellers was sharp enough that it was hard to imagine he’d been unable to play a week before. But as so often happens in football games coached by Kirby Smart, things turned in the middle eight minutes.That’s when the patient pressure of the UGA offensive line began to pay dividends. Georgia engineered a 10 play, 88 yard touchdown drive to take a 10-6 lead. The Red and Black then punched in another Frazier touchdown on their first possession of the second half to run the advantage to 17-6. While it wasn’t quite over at that point, the Bulldogs were never not in control from that point forward. The Garnet and Black churned out 123 yards of total offense on their two first half scoring drives. They scrounged out only 95 yards of offense in the remainder of the game. The Athenians on the other hand poured it on, getting better as the evening wore on. The Dawgs finished with 421 yards of total offense, led by a sterling effort from Gunner Stockton. The Tough Guy from Tiger turned in a 19 of 23 passing performance for 281 yards and a touchdown. Critically he avoided any turnovers, in the process avoiding the one thing that could have given the ‘Cocks the momentum they needed. While Stockton didn’t find any Gamecocks with the ball, he found a whole lot of Bulldogs, completing passes to nine different receivers. Jaden Reddell exploded for 88 yards on 3 receptions, including a 66 yarder. Talyn “Talons” Taylor made another highlight reel catch of 37 yards. Georgia ran right at the Gamecocks then rope-a-doped the Gamecocks with deep strikes, and once those started hitting the result became a fait accompli. LaNorris Sellers appeared to be the Gamecocks’ only hope. In the end, he was a non-factor.

By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th.
